Follow-up for a further 3.5 years10 suggested that long-term treatment with gemfibrozil seemed to postpone coro- nary events for about 5 years. The Veterans Affairs High-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol Intervention Trial (VA-HIT)11 assessed gemfibrozil for the secondary prevention of ischaemic heart dis- ease in 2531 older men (mean age 64 years) whose primary lipid abnormality was a low HDL-cholesterol level. There was an overall reduction of 22% in the incidence of fatal and non-fatal myocardial infarctions and cardiac deaths in the gemfibrozil group compared with the placebo group, with the beneficial ef- fects of gemfibrozil becoming apparent about 2 years after ran- domisation.
